name: Highlands 18

nadir.desc: The nadir view shows a large single-story residential structure with a multi-section tan/adobe-colored roof set within a semi-arid high-desert landscape dominated by scattered juniper trees|A paved driveway connects the property to a road on the east side, looping through a circular turnaround near the front of the structure|A detached structure with a light-colored metal roof sits to the northeast of the main residence, and a basketball court with painted markings is visible on a grassed area to the north|The property has a landscaped lawn on the north and northwest sides, while the surrounding terrain is open desert with no fencing visible.

alpha.desc: The alpha view shows the front of the property from the street side, with the paved road running along the right edge of the view and a paved driveway leading from the road toward the main residence|Multiple juniper trees are distributed across the property and along the driveway approach, which may reduce visibility and clearance for larger vehicles|The main structure is visible in the center-left of the view as a low-profile, multi-section building, and the green lawn area is visible behind and to the left of the residence|The circular driveway turnaround is discernible near the front of the structure.

bravo.desc: The bravo view shows the right side of the property from a position looking toward the rear-left, with dense juniper tree coverage dominating the foreground and mid-ground|The main residence and associated structures are partially visible in the upper-center portion of the view, with the green lawn area visible adjacent to the buildings|The extent of tree coverage on this side significantly limits lateral visibility and access routes from the right.

charlie.desc: The charlie view shows the rear of the property, with the residence visible as a low-profile structure in the center of the view surrounded by dense juniper trees on all sides|A paved or hardscaped area is visible near the structures at the rear|No additional structures, fencing, or access points are clearly observable from this perspective, and the rear of the property transitions directly into open desert terrain with heavy tree coverage that limits rear access.

delta.desc: The delta view shows the left side of the property, with the multi-section main residence and the detached structure with a metal roof both visible in the center-right of the view|The green lawn area is visible between the two structures to the right|Dense juniper trees line the left side and rear of the property, limiting approach and visibility from this direction|A paved surface or hardscaped area connecting portions of the property is visible adjacent to the structures.

considerations: The property is accessed via a single paved driveway off the road to the east, which leads to a circular turnaround in front of the main residence, providing a defined staging and apparatus positioning area. Dense juniper trees throughout the property and along the driveway approach restrict lateral visibility and may limit clearance for larger emergency vehicles. The rear and sides of the property have no visible paved access routes, and off-road approach through desert terrain with scattered trees would be required to reach those areas. The detached structure with the metal roof to the northeast is accessible from the main driveway and turnaround area.
clarifications: Does the driveway and circular turnaround have adequate vertical clearance and surface load capacity for fire apparatus? Is the detached northeast structure used as a garage, and does it have any interior vehicle access? Are there any gates or controlled access points along the driveway between the road and the residence? Are there any utilities, propane tanks, or fuel storage on the property not visible from above? Does the property have a designated address marker or house number visible from the road?
